features.feature: Invisible, Hidden, Print, NoView and ToggleNoView device/interaction decisions
features.source_location: Table167 physical486/printed471 bits1–8; continuation physical487/printed472 bit9 ToggleNoView and fixed-corner prose.
features.source_rule: Invisible applies only to annotation types the processor does not recognize; clear Invisible permits their AP if any. Hidden suppresses display and interaction regardless of type/handler. Print set prints unless Hidden; Print clear never prints; if there are no appearance streams, Print is ignored. NoView suppresses on-screen display and interaction but may print according to Print. ToggleNoView inverts NoView for selection and mouse hovering, making the annotation visible under the pointer/selection.
features.errata: No EC3 correction located that changes these Table 167 flag meanings. #1 changes §12.5.2's fallback cross-reference to §12.5.5/Table 167 bits 1–2, relevant to unknown-type handling but not the bit semantics above.

features.verdict: Core reader flag semantics are strongly covered at model pixels and public printing/viewer paths. Remaining worthwhile gaps are cross-product assertions: ToggleNoView's pointer inversion must not leak into print, and the actual raster export verb should preserve the ADR 1179 policy that Export uses screen flag semantics. These are policy/integration guards, not undiscovered ISO requirements.
features.residuals: No audit of every widget/form state interaction or archive rewrite flag policy. Export behavior for annotation flags is not specified by Table 167: it names screen and printed page only. The exporter follows an explicit product choice in ADR 1179, not a derived mandatory conformance rule.
features.execution: Two new tests PASS: model screen/print/hover cross-product and actual transform RenderPlan PNG. Model/transform all-targets Clippy PASS.
features.parent_assertion_qualification: Existing print_intent matrix and public Command::Print test check display-list marks, not printed pixels. Existing toggle screen test does check literal red/blank pixels. New cross-product checks red/transparent center and transparent exterior; new exporter checks decoded PNG dimensions, literal red/white pixels, exterior white and equality to no-annotation control.
